A while back I asked about hammock ideas for switching from my standard queen size beds to an Indoor hammock.

https://voat.co/v/hammocks/comments/336307

My living space is still under construction, so any pictures I've taken where entirely made of potatoes and much worse than Amazon's pictures anyway. But, this is what I've ordered and been sleeping on for just over a week now.

MobileLink

Non-Mobile Link

So far, I've been really liking it; sleeping soundly throughout the night, no neck/back aches, and still surprisingly able to toss and turn from side to side. I've been sleeping on it the long way and not as shown in the picture, but maybe I'll try that position for a week to compare.

The cotton feels nice, normally I sleep in boxers but too much body heat is lost through the hammock so I'd rather wear sweats and a t-shirt than use an under blanket.

Getting in and out, changing positions, and having my two small dogs join me takes some getting used to; but I wasn't expecting so much freedom to move around. Despite the cocoon wrapping, I'm able to wiggle around into all sorts of positions with no issues with balance or comfort.

The heat loss will require some planning for winter, I'm debating bundling myself up or layering the hammock itself (maybe get an electric blanket into the mix).

The anchor hooks are adjustable to control depth/taughtness, I'm slightly worried I'm sleeping in the wrong direction and maybe stretching it out too quickly but I'm only on the 2nd/3rd hook depth so that could just be natural growing pains.

Overall, $150 for the full hammock and stand was a great find. The stands I was originally looking at were almost $200 on their own. I'm quite happy with the purchase, and will be sure to post another show off picture once I get a living space worth showing off.
